semantics.note: Revision 2 keeps the 'informal read' and information-gap hedges, plus the scope (Tesla and Waymo) and the target of unrestricted everyday use. It is correctly classed as an observation about mid-2022.

contract.note: Fair to his words. 'Anywhere close' has no measure, and he openly frames this as a tentative read. Treating it as a firm availability claim would add a commitment he did not make.

reviews.rationale: This is a hedged, informal judgment about how close Tesla and Waymo were in 2022. He gives no threshold for 'anywhere close', and the contract sets no objective support or contradiction condition. The packet has no evidence. Because the claim is too vague and hedged to score, it is not adjudicable. The case itself is not broken.

semantics.note: 'We just shouldn't expect' is advice about what to expect. The drafter turned it into a categorical 'will not arrive' forecast, which overstates his commitment. 'Any time soon' also sets no deadline. Under the policy a should-statement is normative.

contract.note: Fair. The contract declines to turn advice into a dated nonarrival prediction and declines to invent a deadline for 'any time soon'.

reviews.rationale: This is normative advice about expectations. Even read as a prediction, 'any time soon' has no deadline, so it could not be scored. The packet has no evidence. The claim is not adjudicable, and the case is not broken.
